notes.front: What is the ISC2 Code of Ethics?
notes.back: The ethics code all ISC2 members pledge to uphold; keeping to it strictly is required to hold the certification.
notes.explanation: ISC2 presents certification as a privilege that has to be earned and then kept, and the code is how it is kept.
notes.source: ISC2 Code of Ethics, “Code”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words
notes.example: Like a medical council's code that a doctor must keep to stay registered, but for certified security professionals.

notes.front: How many mandatory canons does the ISC2 Code of Ethics contain?
notes.back: Four.
notes.explanation: ISC2 keeps the canons few and high-level, and says they are not meant to replace a professional's own ethical judgement.
notes.source: ISC2 Code of Ethics, “Code”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: What does Canon I of the ISC2 Code of Ethics require?
notes.back: Protecting society and the common good, the trust and confidence the public needs to have, and the infrastructure.
notes.explanation: ISC2's complaint rules let any member of the public complain about a breach of this canon.
notes.source: ISC2 Code of Ethics, “Code of Ethics Canons”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: What does Canon II of the ISC2 Code of Ethics require?
notes.back: Behaving with honour and honesty, fairly, responsibly and within the law.
notes.explanation: It concerns the member's own personal conduct, and the complaint rules let any member of the public complain about a breach of it.
notes.source: ISC2 Code of Ethics, “Code of Ethics Canons”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: What does Canon III of the ISC2 Code of Ethics require?
notes.back: Giving principals, meaning employers and clients, careful and capable service.
notes.explanation: Principals are the member's employers and the clients who contract with them, and only they may complain about a breach of this canon.
notes.source: ISC2 Code of Ethics, “Code of Ethics Canons”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: What does Canon IV of the ISC2 Code of Ethics require?
notes.back: Helping the profession move forward, and defending it.
notes.explanation: ISC2 treats failing to report another member's breach as a possible breach of this canon.
notes.source: ISC2 Code of Ethics, “Code of Ethics Canons”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: Which three duties does the Code's preamble name alongside the safety and welfare of society?
notes.back: The common good, duty to principals, and duty to one another.
notes.explanation: The preamble gives these as the reason members must hold to the highest ethical standards.
notes.source: ISC2 Code of Ethics, “Code of Ethics Preamble”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: The preamble asks members not only to keep to the highest ethical standards but also to be {{c1::seen}} keeping to them.
notes.explanation: The preamble ties this standard to the safety and welfare of society, and to duties to principals and to one another.
notes.source: ISC2 Code of Ethics, “Code of Ethics Preamble”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: What happens to an ISC2 member who intentionally or knowingly violates the Code?
notes.back: A peer review panel may act against them, and that action can include taking away their certification.
notes.explanation: The preamble makes strict adherence to the Code a condition of certification.
notes.source: ISC2 Code of Ethics, “Code”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: What must an ISC2 member do on observing another member breach the Code?
notes.back: Report it through ISC2's ethics complaint procedure; not doing so can itself count as a breach of Canon IV.
notes.explanation: The Code links a failure to report directly to Canon IV, advancing and protecting the profession.
notes.source: ISC2 Code of Ethics, “Code”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: Are the canons meant to replace a professional's ethical judgement?
notes.back: No. The canons are only broad guidance, so professionals must still use their own ethical judgement.
notes.explanation: The Code says this follows, by necessity, from the canons being high-level guidance.
notes.source: ISC2 Code of Ethics, “Code”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: Who may complain about a breach of Canon I or Canon II?
notes.back: Any member of the public who claims to be injured by the behaviour.
notes.explanation: Standing differs by canon, and complaints are accepted only from those who claim to be injured by the behaviour.
notes.source: ISC2, Ethical Complaint Procedures, “Standing of Complainant”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: Who may complain about a breach of Canon III?
notes.back: Only principals, meaning the member's employers or the clients who contract with them.
notes.explanation: Canon III is the duty of diligent and competent service to principals.
notes.source: ISC2, Ethical Complaint Procedures, “Standing of Complainant”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: Who may complain about a breach of Canon IV?
notes.back: Only fellow professionals: people who hold a professional certification or licence and are bound by a code of ethics.
notes.explanation: By contrast, any member of the public may complain about Canons I and II.
notes.source: ISC2, Ethical Complaint Procedures, “Standing of Complainant”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: In what form must an ethics complaint to ISC2 be made?
notes.back: In writing, as a sworn affidavit; allegations in any other form are not considered.
notes.explanation: The committee is not an investigative body, so it can act only on written evidence given to it voluntarily.
notes.source: ISC2, Ethical Complaint Procedures, “Form of Complaints”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: What must an ethics complaint specify for the committee to consider it?
notes.back: The canon of the Code that was violated.
notes.explanation: A complainant who is unsure may file as best they can or contact the Ethics Committee for help.
notes.source: ISC2, Ethical Complaint Procedures, “Specificity of Complaints”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: If the facts stay disputed and the Ethics Committee cannot reach a conclusion, who gets the benefit of the doubt?
notes.back: The member complained about; where the facts are disputed, it is for the complainant to prove them.
notes.explanation: The committee has no duty to make a finding while the facts remain in dispute.
notes.source: ISC2, Ethical Complaint Procedures, “Disagreement on the Facts”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: When recommending action, which kind of action does the Ethics Committee prefer?
notes.back: The mildest, most cautious action that its findings support.
notes.explanation: The procedures are there to protect the profession's reputation, not to punish certificate holders.
notes.source: ISC2, Ethical Complaint Procedures, “Findings and Recommendations”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: What is the sole purpose ISC2 gives for its ethics complaint procedures?
notes.back: Safeguarding the profession's good name; the procedures are not a tool for pressuring or penalising certificate holders.
notes.explanation: ISC2 adds that publishing the procedures is not meant to invite or encourage complaints.
notes.source: ISC2, Ethical Complaint Procedures, “Preamble”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: Before authorising someone's access to a system, what must an organisation receive under the rules-of-behaviour control?
notes.back: A documented acknowledgement that the person has read, understands and agrees to abide by the rules of behaviour.
notes.explanation: The rules describe each user's responsibilities and expected behaviour for using the information and system, including security and privacy.
notes.evidence: Receive a documented acknowledgment from such individuals, indicating that they have read, understand, and agree to abide by the rules of behavior, before authorizing access
notes.source: SP 800-53 Rev. 5, PL-4 Rules of Behavior
notes.sourceLicence: B · public domain (US Government work)

notes.front: When must users re-acknowledge an organisation's rules of behaviour?
notes.back: At an organisation-defined frequency and/or when the rules are revised or updated.
notes.explanation: The control also requires the organisation to review and update the rules at a frequency it sets.
notes.evidence: Require individuals who have acknowledged a previous version of the rules of behavior to read and re-acknowledge
notes.source: SP 800-53 Rev. 5, PL-4 Rules of Behavior
notes.sourceLicence: B · public domain (US Government work)

notes.front: Besides rules of behaviour, what are two other types of access agreement for organisational users?
notes.back: Any two of: nondisclosure agreements; conflict-of-interest agreements; acceptable use agreements.
notes.explanation: The control describes rules of behaviour as one type of access agreement among these.
notes.evidence: Other types of access agreements include nondisclosure agreements, conflict-of-interest agreements, and acceptable use agreements
notes.source: SP 800-53 Rev. 5, PL-4 Rules of Behavior
notes.sourceLicence: B · public domain (US Government work)

notes.front: A certified consultant agrees to include manual testing in a client's security review, then, short of time, runs only an automated scan and tells the client so. Which canon is most directly at stake?
notes.back: D: Canon III.
notes.explanation: Canon III requires diligent and competent service to principals, and the client is the consultant's principal.
notes.source: ISC2 Code of Ethics, “Code of Ethics Canons”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words
notes.choices:
A) Canon I
B) Canon II
C) Canon IV
D) Canon III
notes.choicesExplained: A is wrong because the harm falls on the client, not on society at large. B is wrong because the consultant is open about the shortfall, so honesty is not what failed. C is wrong because the profession is not the party let down first.

notes.front: A member publicly releases a working attack tool for water-treatment control systems before any operator can patch. Which canon is most directly at stake?
notes.back: B: Canon I.
notes.explanation: Canon I requires protecting society, the common good, public trust and confidence, and the infrastructure.
notes.source: ISC2 Code of Ethics, “Code of Ethics Canons”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words
notes.choices:
A) Canon III
B) Canon I
C) Canon IV
D) None, because no employer is involved
notes.choicesExplained: A is wrong because no principal's service is in question. C is wrong because the main harm is to the public, not the profession. D is wrong because Canon I protects society regardless of any employer.

notes.front: A member lists a degree they never earned on a job application. Which canon is most directly at stake?
notes.back: A: Canon II.
notes.explanation: Canon II requires acting honourably, honestly, justly, responsibly and legally.
notes.source: ISC2 Code of Ethics, “Code of Ethics Canons”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words
notes.choices:
A) Canon II
B) Canon I
C) Canon III
D) Canon IV
notes.choicesExplained: B is wrong because society and infrastructure are not endangered. C is wrong because there is no principal yet. D is closer, but the direct failure is personal dishonesty.

notes.front: A member volunteers to mentor newcomers and speaks at student events about entering the field. Which canon does this most directly serve?
notes.back: B: Canon IV.
notes.explanation: Canon IV asks members to advance and protect the profession.
notes.source: ISC2 Code of Ethics, “Code of Ethics Canons”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words
notes.choices:
A) Canon I
B) Canon IV
C) Canon III
D) Canon II
notes.choicesExplained: A is wrong because the activity is aimed at the field rather than at protecting public infrastructure. D is wrong because it goes beyond personal honesty. C is wrong because no principal is being served.

notes.front: A member learns that a certified colleague sold a client's confidential data. The member would rather stay out of it. What does the Code expect?
notes.back: A: Follow the ethics complaint procedure.
notes.explanation: Members must follow the complaint procedure on observing a breach by another member.
notes.source: ISC2 Code of Ethics, “Code”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words
notes.choices:
A) Follow the ethics complaint procedure
B) Tell the colleague privately and stop there
C) Nothing, since the member was not involved
D) Post the details publicly
notes.choicesExplained: C and B are wrong because members are obliged to follow the complaint procedure on observing a breach, and failing to may breach Canon IV. D is wrong because the procedure, not public exposure, is the required route.

notes.front: A rival firm's owner, who holds no professional certification or licence, files a complaint that a certified member is damaging the profession's reputation. Will ISC2 accept it under Canon IV?
notes.back: D: No, only other certified or licensed professionals bound by a code of ethics may.
notes.explanation: Standing for Canon IV complaints is limited to other professionals who are certified or licensed and subscribe to a code of ethics.
notes.source: ISC2, Ethical Complaint Procedures, “Standing of Complainant”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words
notes.choices:
A) Yes, anyone may complain about any canon
B) Only if the member's employer agrees
C) Yes, if the complaint is sent by email
D) No, only other certified or licensed professionals bound by a code of ethics may
notes.choicesExplained: A is wrong because standing differs by canon. C is wrong because complaints must be sworn affidavits in writing. B is wrong because an employer's agreement plays no part in standing for Canon IV.

notes.front: A contractor's account is set up on Monday, but she has not yet signed the organisation's rules of behaviour. Under the rules-of-behaviour control, what should happen?
notes.back: C: Withhold access until she gives a documented acknowledgement of the rules.
notes.explanation: The control requires a documented acknowledgement of the rules before authorising access to information and the system.
notes.evidence: Receive a documented acknowledgment from such individuals, indicating that they have read, understand, and agree to abide by the rules of behavior, before authorizing access
notes.source: SP 800-53 Rev. 5, PL-4 Rules of Behavior
notes.sourceLicence: B · public domain (US Government work)
notes.choices:
A) Grant read-only access instead
B) Grant access and collect the signature at her annual review
C) Withhold access until she gives a documented acknowledgement of the rules
D) Nothing, because contractors are exempt
notes.choicesExplained: B and A are wrong because the acknowledgement must come before access is authorised. D is wrong because the control covers individuals requiring access to the system.
